body:
## Overview

Implements a complete site-wide footer component with responsive multi-column layout, social media links with hover animations, and copyright information following the cyberpunk design system.

## Changes Made

### New Components

**Footer Component** (`src/components/layout/Footer.tsx`)
- Responsive 4-column layout on desktop that stacks to single column on mobile
- Four main sections: About Subcult, Quick Links, Connect, and Follow Us
- Animated entrance effects using Framer Motion with staggered fade-in
- Dark cyberpunk theme with neon accents matching site design
- Integrated into `App.tsx` to appear on all pages

**SocialLinks Component** (`src/components/layout/SocialLinks.tsx`)
- Reusable component for displaying social media icons
- Text-based icons (𝕏, IG, YT, GH) with hover animations
- Neon cyan glow effect and tooltips on hover using Framer Motion
- Accessible with proper ARIA labels

**Social Configuration** (`src/config/social.ts`)
- Centralized configuration for social media links (Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, GitHub)
- Footer navigation links for all main pages
- Contact information and RSS feed placeholder
- Copyright and license information with dynamic year calculation

### Integration

Modified `App.tsx` to wrap routes in a flex container and add the Footer component at the bottom, ensuring it appears consistently across all pages.

## Features

- **Responsive Design**: Adapts seamlessly from desktop (4 columns) to mobile (1 column)
- **Hover Animations**: Social icons scale and glow with neon cyan effect on hover
- **Tooltips**: Display social handles when hovering over icons
- **Entrance Animations**: Smooth staggered fade-in effects as footer comes into view
- **Type-Safe**: Full TypeScript support using existing `SocialLink` interface
- **Accessible**: Semantic HTML with proper ARIA labels and keyboard navigation
- **Configurable**: Easy to update social links and content via configuration file

## Screenshots

### Desktop View
The footer features a clean 4-column layout with neon-themed section headers matching the site's cyberpunk aesthetic:

![Footer Desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83418e34-ab94-4ac3-8d2c-269272a23a49)

### Hover Effect
Social media icons feature smooth scale animation and neon cyan glow on hover, with tooltips displaying handles:

![Footer Hover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b55d7b27-0df5-4f88-bd35-14addecff1c7)

### Mobile Responsive Layout
On mobile devices, the footer gracefully collapses to a single-column layout:

![Footer Mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0181c4d-f4b2-47a0-b9dd-6c0f9546ba70)

### Consistent Across Pages
Footer appears consistently on all pages with proper spacing:

![About Page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35a211b3-2c2d-46f6-90e2-d264d3d2a787)

## Technical Details

- Uses existing Framer Motion animation utilities from `utils/animations.ts`
- Leverages TailwindCSS theme colors and custom classes (neon-cyan, cyber-black, etc.)
- No additional dependencies required
- Follows project's ESLint and Prettier code style
- All builds and linting checks pass ✅

## Documentation

Added comprehensive README in `src/components/layout/README.md` with usage examples and configuration guide.

body:
Fix https://github.com/bucketeer-io/javascript-client-sdk/issues/272

This prevents event loss in private/incognito mode and ensures all queued events are sent before page closure, even when the event count exceeds the batch size limit.

### Things done

- Flush all events in multiple batches during page unload
- Add automatic page lifecycle listeners (pagehide, visibilitychange, beforeunload)
- Add enableAutoPageLifecycleFlush config option (default: true)
- Reduce default flush interval from 30s to 10s
- Export setupPageLifecycleListeners utility for manual control

---

This pull request introduces automatic event flushing on page lifecycle events (such as navigating away or switching tabs) to help prevent data loss in browser environments. It also lowers the default and minimum event flush intervals for more responsive event delivery, exposes new utilities for page lifecycle management, and improves the robustness of the event flushing logic. Several related configuration options and tests have been updated accordingly.

**Automatic Event Flushing & Page Lifecycle Integration:**

- Added a new configuration option `enableAutoPageLifecycleFlush` (default: `true`) to `BKTConfig` to control whether events are automatically flushed on page lifecycle events (e.g., `pagehide`, `visibilitychange`, `beforeunload`). When enabled, the SDK will attempt to flush pending events before the user leaves or hides the page, reducing the chance of data loss. (`src/BKTConfig.ts`, `src/main.browser.ts`, `package.json`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8337fae3ee192f5326edd7fa03f6e3c045bfad438c75bed8d2aeea3cd8a05eR39-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8337fae3ee192f5326edd7fa03f6e3c045bfad438c75bed8d2aeea3cd8a05eR69) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8337fae3ee192f5326edd7fa03f6e3c045bfad438c75bed8d2aeea3cd8a05eR100) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6bf2e52800778ec01f0bc95b70194d1012563a5d7f3a8a93136743bd9bc6ae1bR11) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6bf2e52800778ec01f0bc95b70194d1012563a5d7f3a8a93136743bd9bc6ae1bL45-R68) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R35-R39)
- Introduced a new utility module `utils/pageLifecycle` that provides `setupPageLifecycleListeners`, `supportsSendBeacon`, and related types for handling page lifecycle events and event flushing in browsers. (`src/utils/pageLifecycle.ts`, [src/utils/pageLifecycle.tsR1-R109](diffhunk://#diff-a2fabfc7d6de5c889a7cb2c95f28a51c15fa092bd7af68d0f0783d795331ff6fR1-R109))
- Exposed the new lifecycle utilities in the public API for advanced/manual usage. (`src/main.browser.ts`, [src/main.browser.tsR31-R35](diffhunk://#diff-6bf2e52800778ec01f0bc95b70194d1012563a5d7f3a8a93136743bd9bc6ae1bR31-R35))

**Event Flushing Behavior Improvements:**

- Modified the `flush()` method in `BKTClientImpl` to repeatedly send events in batches until the event queue is empty, ensuring all pending events are sent even if they exceed the batch size. (`src/BKTClient.ts`, [src/BKTClient.tsR184-R195](diffhunk://#diff-289955f2b149e8c4564ae592985fe8d5c6abdf0afb2c5a9072e83df75fbde68dR184-R195))
- Added and updated tests to verify that `flush()` sends all events in multiple batches and that event flushing works correctly with the new configuration and lifecycle options. (`test/BKTClient.spec.ts`, [test/BKTClient.spec.tsR984-R1064](diffhunk://#diff-8a26a0ff2b910ea091aec9ae7ef2c415bb9402e0c7fa8c7c0bf971289017e429R984-R1064))

**Configuration Defaults and Validation:**

- Lowered the default and minimum `eventsFlushInterval` from 30 seconds to 10 seconds for more frequent event delivery. Updated tests and documentation to reflect this change. (`src/BKTConfig.ts`, `test/BKTConfig.spec.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8337fae3ee192f5326edd7fa03f6e3c045bfad438c75bed8d2aeea3cd8a05eL12-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL25-L34) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL46-L57) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL99-R102) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL177-R184)
- Ensured that `enableAutoPageLifecycleFlush` defaults to `true` when not specified and can be explicitly disabled. Added/updated test coverage for this behavior. (`test/BKTConfig.spec.ts`, [test/BKTConfig.spec.tsR194-R211](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeR194-R211))

**Minor Improvements:**

- Minor code style and formatting improvements in imports and error handling. (`src/BKTClient.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-289955f2b149e8c4564ae592985fe8d5c6abdf0afb2c5a9072e83df75fbde68dL1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-289955f2b149e8c4564ae592985fe8d5c6abdf0afb2c5a9072e83df75fbde68dL13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-289955f2b149e8c4564ae592985fe8d5c6abdf0afb2c5a9072e83df75fbde68dL313-R325) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-289955f2b149e8c4564ae592985fe8d5c6abdf0afb2c5a9072e83df75fbde68dL326-R342) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8a26a0ff2b910ea091aec9ae7ef2c415bb9402e0c7fa8c7c0bf971289017e429L656-R656) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL239-R257) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-a3fd2336f68bf71ea0ee8a2310a07cc6b88bf870522938c2e20e6f45cd83efdeL251-R269)

body:
## Overview

This PR refactors the Purchasing Service to expose its functionality through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling AI agents to interact with the service using standardized MCP tools. The implementation follows the same architectural pattern as the existing `hr-mcp-server` reference implementation.

## Changes Made

### Service Layer (New)
Created a service abstraction layer to encapsulate business logic, making it accessible to both REST API controllers and MCP tools:

- **ISupplierService / SupplierService** - Manages supplier retrieval operations
- **IInquiryService / InquiryService** - Handles offer request processing
- **IOrderService / OrderService** - Processes order placement

### MCP Tools Layer (New)
Added a `Tools/` directory containing:

- **PurchasingTools.cs** - Main MCP tool class with 6 tool methods decorated with `[McpServerTool]` attributes
- **Models.cs** - Supporting collection models for MCP responses

### MCP Tool Methods
The following tools are now available for AI agents:

1. **GetSuppliers** - Retrieves the complete list of suppliers
2. **GetSupplierById** - Fetches a specific supplier by their unique ID
3. **GetSupplierByName** - Retrieves a supplier by company name
4. **GetSuppliersForProduct** - Finds all suppliers offering a specific product
5. **RequestOffer** - Requests pricing and availability offers from suppliers
6. **PlaceOrder** - Places orders with suppliers for specified products

### Program.cs Updates
Minimal modifications to configure the MCP server:

- Registered service implementations with dependency injection
- Configured MCP server with HTTP transport
- Added `MapMcp()` endpoint to expose MCP tools

### MCP Configuration
Created `assets/mcp/purchasing-service.yaml` following the Swagger 2.0 specification with the `x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0` extension, enabling Azure AI agent integration.

## Design Principles

- **Minimal Changes**: Only added new files with minimal modifications to `Program.cs` (14 lines)
- **Backward Compatibility**: All existing REST API controllers remain unchanged and fully functional
- **Architectural Consistency**: Follows the exact pattern established by `hr-mcp-server`
- **Clean Separation**: MCP tools delegate to service layer, maintaining single responsibility
- **Async/Await**: All service methods use async operations for scalability

## Testing

- ✅ Project builds successfully in both Debug and Release configurations
- ✅ Application starts without errors
- ✅ All dependencies resolve correctly
- ✅ No build warnings or errors
- ✅ Existing REST API controllers remain functional

## Files Changed

**New Files (10):**
- `purchasing-service/Services/` - 6 new service interface and implementation files
- `purchasing-service/Tools/` - 2 new MCP tool files
- `assets/mcp/purchasing-service.yaml` - MCP API configuration

**Modified Files (1):**
- `purchasing-service/Program.cs` - Added MCP configuration

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a complete Trading Workspace for BounceHunter/PennyHunter paper trading system, enabling real-time signal monitoring, paper order placement, position tracking, and Phase 2 validation progress visualization.

## Implementation Details

### Backend API Endpoints (8 new endpoints)

Added comprehensive trading API to `src/api/dashboard_api.py`:

**Market Regime Detection** (`GET /api/trading/regime`)
- Real-time SPY/VIX monitoring for penny trading decisions
- Returns regime status (risk_on/risk_off/neutral) with trading permission
- Provides human-readable reasoning for regime determination

**Phase 2 Validation Tracker** (`GET /api/trading/phase2-progress`)
- Tracks progress toward 20-trade validation goal
- Calculates win rate vs 65-75% target range
- Shows total P&L and active trade count
- Determines status (in_progress/success/needs_review)

**Trading Signals Queue** (`GET /api/trading/signals`)
- Quality-filtered gap signals with adjustable threshold (default ≥5.5)
- Integration with advanced filters (liquidity/slippage/runway/sector/volume)
- Returns complete signal details with entry/stop/target prices
- Includes quality score breakdown and filter pass/fail results

**Paper Order Placement** (`POST /api/trading/paper-order`)
- Two-step confirmation workflow to prevent accidental trades
- First call returns order preview with risk/reward calculations
- Second call (with confirmed=true) executes bracket order
- Returns entry, stop, and target order IDs

**Positions Tracking** (`GET /api/trading/positions`)
- Live position data with unrealized P&L
- Portfolio exposure percentage calculations
- Real-time price updates

**Orders Tracking** (`GET /api/trading/orders`)
- All orders with status filtering
- Timestamps for submission and fills
- Support for pagination

**Broker Connectivity** (`GET /api/trading/broker-status`)
- Connection status for all 4 brokers (Paper/Alpaca/Questrade/IBKR)
- Account value and cash balance when connected
- Error messages for disconnected brokers

**Trade Validation** (`POST /api/trading/validate`)
- Mark completed trades for Phase 2 validation
- Updates PennyHunterMemory system
- Appends to cumulative trade history

### Frontend UI Components (6 React/TypeScript components)

**TradingRunboard**
- Session date and current market status
- Market regime card with SPY/VIX metrics and visual indicators
- Phase 2 progress card with animated progress bar
- Win rate tracking with color-coded status
- Auto-refreshes every 60 seconds

**SignalsQueue**
- Grid layout of quality-filtered signals
- Color-coded quality score badges (green/blue/amber/red)
- Advanced filter pass/fail indicators
- Adjustable quality threshold
- Click-to-select for order placement
- Auto-refreshes every 5 minutes

**OrdersPanel**
- Bracket order form with ticker, quantity, prices
- Two-step confirmation modal with risk/reward preview
- Recent orders table with real-time status
- Auto-population from selected signal
- Auto-refreshes every 30 seconds

**PositionsPanel**
- Portfolio summary with total value and P&L
- Positions table with live price updates
- Unrealized P&L with percentage changes
- Exposure visualization with animated bars
- Color-coded gains/losses
- Auto-refreshes every 10 seconds

**BrokerStatus**
- Connection status cards for all brokers
- Account value and cash when connected
- Status indicators (online/offline/not configured)
- Manual refresh capability
- Auto-refreshes every 30 seconds

**TradingWorkspace**
- Main container organizing all panels
- Responsive two-column layout
- Signal-to-order workflow integration
- Professional gradient styling

### Test Coverage

Added comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_trading_api.py` with 16 tests covering:
- All endpoint functionality
- Two-step confirmation workflow
- Quality score filtering logic
- Input validation
- Response time assertions (<5s)
- Phase 2 status transitions
- Broker status validation

### Documentation

**TRADING_WORKSPACE_IMPLEMENTATION.md**
- Complete technical documentation
- Data flow diagrams
- Integration point descriptions
- API endpoint specifications
- Usage instructions
- Future enhancement roadmap

**TRADING_WORKSPACE_QUICK_REF.md**
- Operator quick reference guide
- Daily workflow instructions
- Signal quality gate explanations
- Troubleshooting tips
- Keyboard shortcuts (planned)

## Key Features

✅ **Two-Step Order Confirmation** - Prevents accidental trades with preview/confirm flow  
✅ **Real-Time Updates** - Auto-refreshing data (10s to 5m depending on component)  
✅ **Quality Gates** - Only signals ≥5.5 quality score shown by default  
✅ **Advanced Filters** - 5-module risk filter system with pass/fail indicators  
✅ **Multi-Broker Support** - Paper, Alpaca, Questrade, and IBKR  
✅ **Phase 2 Tracking** - Automated validation progress toward 20-trade goal  
✅ **Live P&L** - Real-time position monitoring with exposure tracking  

## Files Changed

```
17 files changed, 3,876 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

**Backend:**
- `src/api/dashboard_api.py` (+501 lines)

**Frontend:**
- 6 new component pairs (.tsx + .css files, ~2,400 lines total)

**Tests:**
- `tests/test_trading_api.py` (+303 lines)

**Documentation:**
- 2 new documentation files (~741 lines)

## Integration Points

- Integrates with existing broker abstraction layer (`src/bouncehunter/broker.py`)
- Uses PennyHunterMemory for ticker-level statistics tracking
- Updates cumulative trade history for Phase 2 validation
- Connects with advanced filter engine for signal validation
- Compatible with all existing scanner and regime detection systems

## Testing

All 16 tests pass successfully and cover:
- API endpoint functionality
- Two-step confirmation flow
- Data validation and filtering
- Response time requirements
- Status transition logic

## Deployment

**Start API:**
```bash
uvicorn src.api.dashboard_api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --reload
```

**Start Dashboard:**
```bash
cd dashboard && npm install && npm run dev
```

**Access:** `http://localhost:5173`

## Acceptance Criteria

All requirements from the issue have been met:
- ✅ Runboard displays live regime and Phase 2 metrics
- ✅ Signals queue filters by quality and shows filter pass/fail
- ✅ Paper orders can be placed with two-step confirmation
- ✅ Positions update live (via polling, SSE planned)
- ✅ Phase 2 progress card increments on validation
- ✅ Broker connectivity status displayed for all brokers
- ✅ Integration with BounceHunter/PennyHunter scanners complete

## Future Enhancements

- SSE support for true real-time updates without polling
- Trade journal component for detailed notes and screenshots
- Order modification capabilities (cancel/replace)
- Risk calculator with position sizing recommendations
- Trade replay and backtest comparison features

---

This implementation provides a complete, production-ready trading workspace for Phase 2 validation of the BounceHunter/PennyHunter strategy. The system is fully tested, documented, and ready for daily paper trading operations.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>aspect-build/rules_js (aspect_rules_js)</summary>

### [`v2.7.0`](https://redirect.github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/releases/tag/v2.7.0)

Many companies are successfully building with rules\_js.
If you're getting value from the project, please let us know!
Just comment on our [Adoption Discussion](https://redirect.github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/discussions/1000).

#### Using Bzlmod with Bazel 6:

Add to your `MODULE.bazel` file:

```starlark
bazel_dep(name = "aspect_rules_js", version = "2.7.0")

####### Node.js version #########

### By default you get the node version from DEFAULT_NODE_VERSION in @​rules_nodejs//nodejs:repositories.bzl
### Optionally you can pin a different node version:
bazel_dep(name = "rules_nodejs", version = "6.3.0")
node = use_extension("@​rules_nodejs//nodejs:extensions.bzl", "node", dev_dependency = True)
node.toolchain(node_version = "18.14.2")

#################################

npm = use_extension("@​aspect_rules_js//npm:extensions.bzl", "npm", dev_dependency = True)

npm.npm_translate_lock(
    name = "npm",
    pnpm_lock = "//:pnpm-lock.yaml",
    verify_node_modules_ignored = "//:.bazelignore",
)

use_repo(npm, "npm")

pnpm = use_extension("@​aspect_rules_js//npm:extensions.bzl", "pnpm")

### Allows developers to use the matching pnpm version, for example:
### bazel run -- @​pnpm --dir /home/runner/work/rules_js/rules_js install
use_repo(pnpm, "pnpm")
```

#### Using WORKSPACE

Paste this snippet into your `WORKSPACE` file:

```starlark
load("@​bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
    name = "aspect_rules_js",
    sha256 = "9dd50d3bacb2fe1d4a721098981b70290fe9ac56d3625791f490d2ab94f2cac6",
    strip_prefix = "rules_js-2.7.0",
    url = "https://github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/releases/download/v2.7.0/rules_js-v2.7.0.tar.gz",
)

load("@​aspect_rules_js//js:repositories.bzl", "rules_js_dependencies")

rules_js_dependencies()

load("@​aspect_rules_js//js:toolchains.bzl", "DEFAULT_NODE_VERSION", "rules_js_register_toolchains")

rules_js_register_toolchains(node_version = DEFAULT_NODE_VERSION)

load("@​aspect_rules_js//npm:repositories.bzl", "npm_translate_lock")

npm_translate_lock(
    name = "npm",
    npmrc = "//:.npmrc",
    pnpm_lock = "//:pnpm-lock.yaml",
    verify_node_modules_ignored = "//:.bazelignore",
)

load("@​npm//:repositories.bzl", "npm_repositories")

npm_repositories()
```

#### What's Changed

- test: use rules\_shell for sh\_\* in tests by [@​jbedard](https://redirect.github.com/jbedard) in [#​2390](https://redirect.github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/pull/2390)

- Remove host\_yq from label\_store by [@​dzbarsky](https://redirect.github.com/dzbarsky) in [#​2398](https://redirect.github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/pull/2398)
- Changes by create-pull-request action by [@​github-actions](https://redirect.github.com/github-actions)\[bot] in [#​2394](https://redirect.github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/pull/2394)

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/sonidovivoes/agent-runs/68f89fc84de6c8b2091816bc

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** The contact form is not working - Netlify is not detecting the form and no submissions are being received. Please diagnose and fix: 1) Check the FormBlock component to ensure the form element has data-netlify="true" and data-netlify-honeypot="bot-fie...

✅ **Result:** The contact form has been fixed to work properly with Netlify Forms. Several critical issues were identified and resolved:

The form name attribute was changed from the dynamic `elementId` value ("contact-form") to the static value "contact" to match Netlify's requirements. This ensures Netlify can properly identify and route form submissions.

The hidden `form-name` input value was updated to match the form name attribute, now both set to "contact" instead of using the dynamic `elementId` variable.

The bot-field honeypot was moved outside the dynamic fields container and wrapped in a hidden paragraph element to prevent it from being rendered as a visible form field. A filter was added to the fields mapping to skip the bot-field if it appears in the fields array, ensuring it's only rendered in the dedicated hidden location.

A static HTML form was created in `/public/forms.html` to allow Netlify's build bot to detect the form at build time. This is essential for Next.js applications because Netlify Forms detection requires parsing HTML files during the build process, but Next.js renders forms dynamically with JavaScript. The static form includes all the same field names and Netlify attributes as the React component.

The FormBlock component already had the required Netlify attributes in place: `data-netlify="true"`, `data-netlify-honeypot="bot-field"`, and `method="POST"`. All form inputs have proper name attributes that match what Netlify expects. The custom JavaScript form submission handler correctly sends data to Netlify using the proper format (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).

These changes ensure that Netlify will detect the form during builds and properly process submissions sent from the contact page.

author: yode17
body:
Overview
This PR introduces the ColdChain smart contract, a comprehensive solution for tracking temperature-sensitive cargo shipments on the Stacks blockchain with automatic insurance payouts when cold chain integrity is compromised.

 Problem Statement
Pharmaceutical and food transport industries face significant losses due to temperature excursions during shipment. Current solutions lack transparent, automated mechanisms for verifying cold chain compliance and processing insurance claims. This contract provides an immutable, trustless system for temperature monitoring and claim settlement.

 Solution
The ColdChain contract enables:
 Creation of insured shipments with defined temperature ranges
 Realtime temperature recording with automatic cold chain breach detection
 Immutable temperature history for audit trails
 Automatic insurance claim processing when temperature thresholds are violated
 Complete shipment lifecycle management

 Key Features
 Shipment Management: Create shipments with origin, destination, temperature parameters, and insurance amounts
 Temperature Monitoring: Record temperature readings that automatically trigger cold chain breach detection
 Automatic Detection: Contract automatically flags shipments when temperatures exceed acceptable ranges
 Insurance Claims: Streamlined claim process for recipients when cold chain is broken
 Audit Trail: Complete immutable history of all temperature readings and claims
 Status Tracking: Shipments progress through active → coldchain broken/completed → claimed states

 Technical Details
 Uses Clarity maps for efficient data storage and retrieval
 Implements proper error handling with descriptive error codes
 Supports multiple temperature readings per shipment
 Prevents duplicate insurance claims
 Validates all state transitions and permissions

 Testing
Contract passes `clarinet check` without errors or warnings. All functions have been validated for type safety and logical correctness.

 Impact
This enables trustless, automated insurance payouts for temperature-sensitive cargo, reducing fraud, accelerating claim settlement, and providing transparency to all parties in the supply chain.

author: mvdbeek
body:
by avoiding left outer join.
The extra subquery is an sqlalchemy artifact optimized away by the query planner.

The improved query is this:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE collection_hierarchy(collection_id, depth_level) AS (
    SELECT dataset_collection_element.dataset_collection_id AS collection_id, 0 AS depth_level
    FROM dataset_collection_element
    JOIN history_dataset_association ON dataset_collection_element.hda_id = history_dataset_association.id
    WHERE history_dataset_association.dataset_id = 134996190

    UNION

    SELECT dataset_collection_element.dataset_collection_id AS collection_id, 0 AS depth_level
    FROM dataset_collection_element
    JOIN library_dataset_dataset_association ON dataset_collection_element.ldda_id = library_dataset_dataset_association.id
    WHERE library_dataset_dataset_association.dataset_id = 134996190
    UNION ALL

    SELECT parent_dce.dataset_collection_id AS collection_id, ch.depth_level + 1 AS depth_level
    FROM dataset_collection_element AS parent_dce
    INNER JOIN collection_hierarchy AS ch ON parent_dce.child_collection_id = ch.collection_id
    WHERE ch.depth_level < 50
)
SELECT collection_id
FROM collection_hierarchy
ORDER BY collection_id;
```

while before it was:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE collection_hierarchy(collection_id, depth_level) AS (
    SELECT dataset_collection_element.dataset_collection_id AS collection_id, 0 AS depth_level
    FROM dataset_collection_element
    LEFT OUTER JOIN history_dataset_association ON dataset_collection_element.hda_id = history_dataset_association.id
    LEFT OUTER JOIN library_dataset_dataset_association ON dataset_collection_element.ldda_id = library_dataset_dataset_association.id
    WHERE history_dataset_association.dataset_id = 134996190 OR library_dataset_dataset_association.dataset_id = 134996190

    UNION ALL

    SELECT parent_dce.dataset_collection_id AS collection_id, ch.depth_level + 1 AS depth_level
    FROM dataset_collection_element AS parent_dce, collection_hierarchy AS ch
    WHERE parent_dce.child_collection_id = ch.collection_id AND ch.depth_level < 50
)
SELECT collection_id
FROM collection_hierarchy
ORDER BY collection_id
```

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR adds specialized package installation options for research and vision processing workflows to the setup-python action. These features streamline the setup process for data science, machine learning, and neural signal processing environments.

## New Features

### Researcher Tools

A new `researcher-tools` boolean input automatically installs commonly used data science and research packages:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-python@v6
  with:
    python-version: '3.13'
    researcher-tools: true
```

**Installed packages:** numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, jupyter, jupyterlab, scikit-learn, seaborn

This eliminates the need to manually specify these common packages and provides a consistent research environment setup.

### Vision Brain Wave Control

A new `vision-control` input enables specialized environments for computer vision and neural processing with three configuration levels:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-python@v6
  with:
    python-version: '3.13'
    vision-control: 'full'  # Options: basic, advanced, full
```

**Configuration Levels:**
- **`basic`**: Essential image processing (opencv-python, pillow)
- **`advanced`**: Adds deep learning frameworks (tensorflow, torch)
- **`full`**: Complete suite including torchvision, keras, scikit-image, mne (EEG/MEG analysis), and pyeeg (brain wave analysis)

Each level automatically configures environment variables for optimal performance:
- Sets `VISION_CONTROL_ENABLED` and `VISION_CONTROL_LEVEL`
- Configures thread counts (`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`) for advanced/full levels
- Optimizes deep learning frameworks (`TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL`, `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK`) for full level

### Combined Usage

Both features can be used together for comprehensive research environments:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-python@v6
  with:
    python-version: '3.13'
    researcher-tools: true
    vision-control: 'full'
    cache: 'pip'
```

## Implementation Details

- **New modules:** `src/researcher-tools.ts` and `src/vision-control.ts`
- **Integration:** Modified `src/setup-python.ts` to invoke new features after Python setup
- **Error handling:** Graceful degradation with warnings if package installation fails
- **Version management:** Uses `pip install --upgrade` to ensure latest security patches

## Testing

- Added comprehensive test suites for both features (14 new tests)
- All 220 tests passing
- Code coverage maintained at 84%
- Example workflow provided in `docs/examples/researcher-tools-example.yml`

## Security

- CodeQL scan: No vulnerabilities detected
- All packages install latest versions by default for security patches
- Documentation includes recommendations for production use with pinned versions

## Documentation

- Updated README.md with usage examples and security considerations
- Added example workflows demonstrating various use cases
- Included notes about version management for production environments

## Backward Compatibility

These are opt-in features with no impact on existing workflows. Both inputs default to disabled/empty, maintaining full backward compatibility.

---

Resolves the request for researcher tools and vision brain wave control options in setup-python workflows.

This commit addresses the issue where users see "Secrets in snapshot:" with no secrets being returned when using the --list flag.

Changes:
- Add --list-all flag to show all keys in the snapshot for debugging
- Improve --list output to show count of secrets found
- Add helpful tip when no secrets are found to guide users to use --list-all
- Enhance error message when "key" bucket is not found in snapshot
- Add troubleshooting section to README documenting the new debug workflow
- Update command-line flags documentation

The --list-all flag helps users diagnose why secrets aren't being found by:
1. Verifying the snapshot contains data
2. Checking if secrets are stored under the expected /registry/secrets/ prefix
3. Confirming the snapshot is a valid etcd v3 snapshot
4. Identifying if secrets are stored under a different path

All existing tests pass. The new functionality provides better visibility into snapshot contents and helps users troubleshoot their specific etcd configurations.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR adds comprehensive input validation to the character sheet tool using `react-hook-form`. The implementation provides immediate, user-friendly feedback for invalid inputs while maintaining minimal code overhead through reusable helper functions.

## Problem

The character sheet previously had no validation on user inputs, which could lead to:
- Invalid character data being saved (e.g., negative resolve values, empty required fields)
- Poor user experience with no feedback on data entry errors
- Potential data integrity issues when syncing with Firebase

## Solution

Implemented a validation system that:
1. **Uses `react-hook-form`** for declarative validation rules integrated with MUI components
2. **Provides helper functions** (`getTextFieldProps`, `getSelectProps`) to minimize validation wiring overhead
3. **Avoids wrapper components** by leveraging MUI's native `error` and `helperText` props
4. **Includes reusable validation rules** that can be easily composed

## Implementation Details

### Helper Functions

Created validation utilities in `src/features/CharacterSheet/utils/formValidation.ts`:

```typescript
// Simple integration - just spread the helper function result
<TextField
  {...getTextFieldProps(
    register('name', validationRules.required('Name')),
    errors.name
  )}
  label="Name"
/>
```

### Validation Rules

Declarative, composable validation rules:

```typescript
// Single rule
register('resolve', validationRules.numberRange(0, 3, 'Resolve'))

// Combined rules
register('name', validationRules.combine(
  validationRules.required('Name'),
  validationRules.stringLength(1, 100, 'Name')
))
```

### Example Implementations

Implemented validation in two tabs as examples:

**StatisticsTab:**
- Resolve field: number input with range validation (0-3)
- Attribute selects: required field validation

**PersonalTab:**
- Name field: required + length validation (1-100 characters)
- Folk/Upbringing fields: max length validation (50 characters)

## Screenshots

### Statistics Tab
Character attributes and resolve field with validation support:

![Statistics Tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2392b3bd-cdc9-4c07-97eb-5f24d8c73fd0)

### Personal Tab
Character information fields with validation:

![Personal Tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/beffbbfe-fca9-4ffd-bf26-fffd626fe103)

## Testing

- ✅ Added 17 comprehensive tests for validation utilities
- ✅ All existing tests pass (262 total tests)
- ✅ Build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Manually verified validation in browser

## Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation in `src/features/CharacterSheet/VALIDATION.md` including:
- Complete API reference for helper functions
- Validation rules catalog with examples
- Best practices and migration guide
- Accessibility considerations
- Future enhancement suggestions

## Key Features

- **Zero wrapper components** - Direct MUI integration via helper functions
- **Type-safe** - Full TypeScript support with proper types from react-hook-form
- **Minimal overhead** - Simple spread operator usage
- **Flexible** - Easy to compose multiple validation rules
- **User-friendly** - Clear, contextual error messages with field names
- **Accessible** - Proper ARIA attributes automatically applied (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`)

## Migration Path

Other character sheet fields can easily adopt validation using the same pattern:

```typescript
// 1. Add useForm hook
const { register, formState: { errors }, setValue } = useForm()

// 2. Sync with character data
useEffect(() => {
  setValue('fieldName', character.fieldValue)
}, [character.fieldValue, setValue])

// 3. Add validation to input
<TextField
  {...getTextFieldProps(
    register('fieldName', validationRules.required()),
    errors.fieldName
  )}
  // ... rest of props
/>
```

## Future Enhancements

The validation system is designed to be easily extended:
- Additional validation rules can be added to `validationRules`
- Server-side validation integration
- Form-level validation for cross-field dependencies
- Async validation for uniqueness checks

## Breaking Changes

None. This is purely additive - existing functionality remains unchanged.

body:
## Add input validation to character sheet tool using react-hook-form and Yup

### Summary
Successfully integrated `react-hook-form` with `Yup` schema validation for the character sheet tool. The implementation provides user-friendly validation feedback without introducing wrapper components, using helper utilities and MUI component validation properties directly.

### Implementation Details

#### ✅ Completed Tasks

- [x] Install react-hook-form, yup, and @hookform/resolvers dependencies
- [x] Create validation helper utilities for MUI components
  - [x] Create helper function for TextField validation props (`getTextFieldProps`)
  - [x] Create helper function for Select validation props (`getSelectProps`)
  - [x] Create helper function for number field validation props (`getNumberFieldProps`)
  - [x] Create validation schemas using Yup for different field types
  - [x] Create comprehensive tests for validation utilities (25 tests, all passing)
- [x] Integrate react-hook-form into PersonalTab (example 1: text inputs)
  - [x] Convert all PersonalField usages to validated TextField components
  - [x] Add validation for name, folk, upbringing, background, motivation fields
  - [x] Add validation for height, weight, age fields
  - [x] Add validation for description and notes fields
  - [x] Update dialog handlers to sync with form state using `reset()`
- [x] Integrate react-hook-form into StatisticsTab (example 2: number inputs)
  - [x] Add validation for HP field inputs (current, temp, max modifier)
  - [x] Use Controller component for complex number field validation with dynamic rules
- [x] Add validation for skill XP spending (per user request)
  - [x] Create `getCharacterLevel` function to calculate level from spent XP
  - [x] Create `calculateMaxXpPerSkill` function based on character level
  - [x] Create `createSkillXpSchema` for dynamic skill XP validation
  - [x] Integrate validation into SkillsTab with centralized form for all skills
  - [x] Validation enforces max XP per skill based on spent XP (character level)
  - [x] Uses spent XP (not total XP) to calculate level caps
  - [x] Dynamic validation that updates as user spends XP
  - [x] **Ultra-short error messages**: Changed from "Max 16 (Lvl 6)" to just "max 16"
  - [x] **Cross-field revalidation**: All skill XP fields revalidate when any skill changes
- [x] Test validation behavior
  - [x] Create tests for validation helper utilities
  - [x] Add tests for skill XP validation functions
  - [x] Update tests for ultra-shortened error messages
  - [x] Verify all existing tests still pass (270 tests passing)
  - [x] Build project successfully
- [x] Documentation
  - [x] Add comprehensive validation documentation (VALIDATION_README.md)
  - [x] Include code comments explaining validation approach
  - [x] Document helper functions, validation rules, and usage patterns
  - [x] Provide troubleshooting guide and best practices
- [x] Final verification
  - [x] Run all tests (270 tests passing)
  - [x] Build project successfully

### Recent Improvements

**Ultra-Short Error Messages (Latest Change):**
- Changed from "Max 16 (Lvl 6)" to just "max 16"
- Removed level information to make message as short as possible
- Error messages now fit comfortably within the narrow XP input field width
- Maintains clarity while being extremely compact

**Cross-Field Revalidation:**
- Created a single `useForm` instance for all skills in the SkillsTab
- When any skill's XP changes, all skills automatically revalidate with updated totals
- Validation dynamically calculates total spent XP from all form fields during validation
- Ensures validation is always accurate as users distribute XP across skills

### Validation Examples

#### Example 1: Text Field Validation (PersonalTab)
The Name field demonstrates required field validation with clear error messages.

#### Example 2: Number Field Validation (HpField)
The Current HP field demonstrates numeric validation with dynamic constraints.

#### Example 3: Skill XP Validation (SkillsTab)
The skill XP fields demonstrate cross-field validation with ultra-short error messages.

**Error message format:**
- **Before**: "Max 16 (Lvl 6)"
- **After**: "max 16"

This change ensures the error message fits within the narrow XP input field without wrapping to multiple lines.

### Key Features

1. **No Wrapper Components**: Direct integration with MUI components using helper functions
2. **Type-Safe**: Full TypeScript support with proper type inference from Yup schemas
3. **Minimal Overhead**: Each validated field requires only a few extra lines of code
4. **User-Friendly**: Clear, actionable, **ultra-short** error messages
5. **Performance**: Minimal re-renders using react-hook-form's optimized approach
6. **Cross-Field Validation**: All skill XP fields revalidate together when any changes
7. **Validation Modes**: 
   - `onBlur` for text fields (don't interrupt typing)
   - `onChange` for number fields (immediate feedback)
8. **Comprehensive Rules**: Pre-defined validation rules using Yup schemas
9. **Extensible**: Easy to add custom validation rules as needed

### Validation Rules Implemented

- **Name**: Required, 1-50 characters
- **Short Text**: Max 100 characters (folk, upbringing, background, motivation)
- **Physical Measurements**: Max 30 characters (height, weight)
- **Age**: Max 20 characters
- **Description**: Max 1000 characters
- **Notes**: Max 5000 characters
- **HP**: Min 0, must be a valid number, max enforced dynamically
- **Skill XP**: Min 0, max based on character level (calculated from total spent XP)

### Files Changed

- **Modified**: `src/features/CharacterSheet/utils/validation.ts` - Shortened error message format
- **Modified**: `src/features/CharacterSheet/utils/__tests__/validation.test.ts` - Updated test assertions
- **Previously modified**: PersonalTab, HpField, SkillsTab with validation integration

### Testing

- ✅ All 270 existing tests pass
- ✅ 25 tests for validation utilities
- ✅ Build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Error messages are user-friendly, accessible, and extremely concise

### Acceptance Criteria Met

✅ All editable fields in Personal tab validated using react-hook-form with Yup
✅ HP fields in Statistics tab validated using react-hook-form with Yup
✅ Skill XP fields in Skills tab validated using react-hook-form with Yup
✅ No wrapper components introduced for validation
✅ Helper functions exist to set up MUI validation props efficiently
✅ `react-hook-form`, `yup`, and `@hookform/resolvers` added as dependencies
✅ PR includes example usage for text inputs (Personal tab), number inputs (HP field), and cross-field validation (Skill XP)
✅ Error messages are user-friendly, accessible, and ultra-short ("max 16" format)
✅ All skill XP fields revalidate when any of them changes
✅ Documentation reflects new validation approach

body:
Add ProcessId property to CoreWebView2ProcessFailedEventArgs4

This API extends ProcessFailedEventArgs to include the process ID of the failed process, enabling applications to:
- Correlate process failures with running process data from the ProcessInfo API
- Collect process-specific diagnostic information for logging and telemetry
- Analyze crash dumps for specific processes
- Better track and respond to failures in multi-renderer scenarios

The process ID is only available if the process has started and ended unexpectedly. For other failure types, the process ID value will be 0.

author: wuxibin89
body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix a bug introduce in https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/3285. Currently the initialization steps are:
1. **build actor**:  init model and optimizer, then offload to cpu
2. **build rollout**: init model and kv cache
3. **switch to `trainer_mode`**: discard rollout weight and kv cache, load actor model and optimizer to gpu
4. **load_checkpoint**: if checkpoint exists, load model and optimizer from checkpoint, then offload to cpu
5. **switch to `rollout_mode`**: load actor model to gpu, resume rollout weight and sync weight, then offload actor model to cpu and resume kv cache
6. **generate_sequences**

The bug is step 4: if checkpoint doesn't exists, then this step is skipped, leading to actor and optimizer both remain in gpu(from step 3), which may cause step 5 cuda oom.

author: dimadesu
body:
Root Cause:

```ts
enum class EndpointType(@StringRes val id: Int) {
    TS_FILE(R.string.to_ts_file),     // id = 2131558471 (changes between builds!)
    FLV_FILE(R.string.to_flv_file),   // id = 2131558472 (changes between builds!)
    SRT(R.string.to_srt),             // id = 2131558473 (changes between builds!)
    ...
}
```

The EndpointType enum was using Android string resource IDs as the enum ID values:

The Problem:

- Resource IDs are generated at compile time and can change between builds
- When you save "2131558473" (SRT) to SharedPreferences
- After a rebuild, resource IDs get regenerated:
  - R.string.to_flv_file might now be 2131558473 (your old saved value!)
  - R.string.to_srt might now be 2131558480
- So fromId(2131558473) now returns FLV_FILE instead of SRT! 💥

The Solution:

- Changed enum to use stable integer constants (0-7) instead of resource IDs
- Separated label resource ID into labelResId property
- Fixed all preference default checks from .entry == null to .value.isNullOrEmpty()

Changes Made:

✅ EndpointType.kt - Use stable IDs (0-7) instead of resource IDs
✅ SettingsFragment.kt - Updated to use labelResId for display
✅ Fixed all preference reset bugs (endpoint, video encoder, profile, level, audio settings)

Impact:

Endpoint type will no longer randomly change after app updates
All preference settings will now persist correctly

## Overview

Comprehensive code quality audit and optimization performed on the Kindergarten Race Game codebase. This PR addresses code quality issues through console logging cleanup, enhanced TypeScript strictness, and improved code organization.

## Changes Made

### 1. Console Logging Optimization

**Problem:** Production builds included 13 unwrapped `console.log()` statements that expose debug information and add unnecessary runtime overhead.

**Solution:** Wrapped all console.log statements with `if (import.meta.env.DEV)` guards to ensure they only execute during development.

**Files Modified:**
- `src/lib/sound-manager.ts` - 11 debug statements wrapped
- `src/components/QuickDebug.tsx` - 1 debug statement wrapped  
- `src/App.tsx` - 1 fullscreen error log wrapped

**Impact:** Cleaner production builds with no debug logging overhead, improved performance, and reduced bundle size.

### 2. TypeScript Compiler Strictness

**Problem:** TypeScript compiler was not enforcing checks for unused variables and parameters, potentially allowing dead code.

**Solution:** Enhanced `tsconfig.json` with stricter compiler options:
```json
"noUnusedLocals": true,
"noUnusedParameters": true
```

**Impact:** Better code quality enforcement, earlier bug detection during compilation, and encouragement of cleaner code practices.

### 3. Code Organization - Constants Extraction

**Problem:** The `sound-manager.ts` file contained 891 lines with a large embedded constant definition (`SENTENCE_TEMPLATES` - 157 lines) making it harder to maintain.

**Solution:** Extracted educational sentence templates to a dedicated constants file.

**New File:**
- `src/lib/constants/sentence-templates.ts` - 165 lines of well-organized template definitions

**Modified:**
- `src/lib/sound-manager.ts` - Reduced from 891 to 755 lines (-15% reduction)

**Impact:** Improved modularity, easier maintenance and updates, better separation of concerns, and potential for reuse.

- File organization structure

body:
This PR implements a complete podcast feed filtering service using Python's Litestar framework, fulfilling all requirements specified in the issue.

## Overview

PodFilter is a web service that allows users to import RSS podcast feeds, apply custom filtering rules to remove unwanted episodes, and export the filtered feeds for use in podcast applications.

## Key Features Implemented

### 🔐 User Authentication System
- JWT-based authentication with secure token generation
- User registration and login functionality with bcrypt password hashing
- Protected routes requiring authentication
- Session management with proper logout functionality

### 📡 RSS Feed Management
- Single RSS feed URL import capability
- OPML file upload support for importing multiple feeds
- Feed parsing using the `feedparser` library
- Episode metadata extraction and storage

### 🎯 Episode Filtering System
- Custom filtering rules based on episode titles and descriptions
- Support for both text matching and regex patterns
- Include/exclude filtering actions
- User-specific filter management

### 📤 Export Capabilities
- Filtered RSS feed generation and export
- OPML export for importing into podcast applications
- Custom RSS XML generation with proper formatting

### 🌐 Web Interface
- Responsive Bootstrap 5 UI design
- Static landing page for non-authenticated users
- Interactive dashboard for authenticated users
- Clean navigation and user experience

## Technical Architecture

**Backend:**
- **Framework**: Litestar (modern async Python web framework)
- **Database**: SQLite with async SQLAlchemy 2.0+
- **Authentication**: JWT tokens with bcrypt password hashing
- **API Design**: RESTful endpoints with `/api` prefix

**Database Schema:**
- `users` - User accounts with secure credentials
- `feeds` - RSS feed information and metadata
- `episodes` - Individual podcast episodes with filtering status
- `filter_rules` - User-defined filtering criteria

**Security:**
- Zero vulnerabilities detected via CodeQL analysis
- Secure password storage with bcrypt hashing
- JWT token-based authentication
- Input validation using Pydantic models
- SQL injection protection via SQLAlchemy ORM

## Screenshots

**Landing Page for Non-Authenticated Users:**
![Homepage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8911de98-e257-4789-85ca-a6e6226d7264)

**Dashboard for Authenticated Users:**
![Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94612e96-2b0d-42c6-bf61-8f0353247024)

## Requirements Fulfillment

✅ **User login system** - Complete JWT-based authentication  
✅ **RSS feed import** - Single URL and OPML file support  
✅ **Episode filtering** - Advanced rule-based filtering system  
✅ **Export functionality** - RSS and OPML export capabilities  
✅ **Static content serving** - Landing page for unauthenticated users  

## Usage

1. Visit the service homepage
2. Register a new account or login with existing credentials
3. Access the dashboard to manage feeds and filters
4. Import RSS feeds individually or via OPML file upload
5. Create filtering rules to remove unwanted episodes
6. Export filtered feeds as RSS or OPML for use in podcast apps

The service is now fully functional and ready for production deployment with comprehensive security measures and a complete feature set for podcast feed management.

body:
This PR applies automated optimisations to `.github/workflows/ci-cd-aws.yaml` to improve CI/CD pipeline efficiency.

**Correlation ID**: `25084878`

## Issues Detected
1. Repeated steps for checking out code and setting up Node.js in multiple jobs, leading to redundant execution time.
2. Installing dependencies in each job, which can be time-consuming and inefficient.
3. Using 'npm install' instead of 'npm ci' for production builds, which is less reliable for consistent builds.
4. Lack of caching for Docker layers, which can slow down the build process.
5. Snyk is installed globally in the security-scan job, which adds unnecessary overhead.
6. Hardcoded sleep times for deployment stabilization, which can lead to unnecessary waiting.

## Changes Applied
1. Use a single job for checking out code and setting up Node.js, and pass the environment to subsequent jobs using job outputs.
2. Implement caching for npm dependencies using the GitHub Actions cache action to speed up installations.
3. Replace 'npm install' with 'npm ci' in the build job to ensure a clean and reproducible build environment.
4. Optimize Docker builds by leveraging Docker layer caching and multi-stage builds to reduce image size and build time.
5. Install Snyk as a dev dependency in the project and run it directly from the local node_modules instead of installing it globally.
6. Use AWS CLI commands to check the deployment status instead of hardcoded sleep, allowing for dynamic wait times.

## Expected Improvement
Estimated reduction in total workflow time by 30-50%, leading to faster feedback loops and more efficient resource usage.

body:
[COPILOT GENERATED]

This PR introduces **comprehensive parallelization improvements** across the deepUMIcaller pipeline, significantly enhancing performance and scalability for large duplex sequencing datasets. The changes enable multi-level parallel processing throughout the workflow while maintaining resource efficiency and result accuracy.

---

### 🚀 Core Parallelization Features

#### 1. **Multi-File Per Sample Input Support** (Lane-Level Parallelization)
- **New capability**: Process multiple FASTQ files per sample in parallel
- Added input_example_lanes.csv demonstrating lane-specific input format
- Automatic grouping and merging of technical replicates using `groupTuple()` operations
- Enables efficient processing of multi-lane sequencing runs where samples are split across multiple files
- **Workflow logic**: 
  - When `params.splitted_original_sample = true`, BAMs are grouped by `meta.sample` and merged per sample
  - Prevents redundant sequential processing of lanes from the same biological sample

#### 2. **Chromosome-Based Parallelization** (`--split_by_chrom`)
- **New module**: `SPLITBAMCHROM` splits aligned BAMs by chromosome for parallel consensus calling
- **Workflow integration**: Optional chromosome splitting at two key stages:
  1. **Before UMI grouping** (line 262-288 in deepumicaller.nf): Splits merged BAMs by chromosome, processes each independently through `GROUPREADSBYUMI` → `CALLDUPLEXCONSENSUSREADS`
  2. **Before filtering** (line 343+): Merges chromosome-split results for downstream analysis
- **Species support**: Automatic chromosome detection for `homo_sapiens` (chr1-22, X, Y, M) and `mus_musculus` (chr1-19, X, Y, M)
- **Output**: Per-chromosome BAMs (e.g., `sample.chr1.bam`, `sample.chr2.bam`) plus `unknown.bam` for unmapped/HLA/EBV sequences
- **Statistics**: Generates detailed filtering stats per chromosome including read counts and paired/unpaired ratios
- **Benefits**:
  - Parallel consensus calling across chromosomes (25+ parallel jobs for human samples)
  - Reduced memory per job (processing 1/25th of genome per task)
  - Faster wall-clock time for large datasets
  - **Same final results** as non-split processing (validated in tests)

#### 3. **Multi-threaded AS-XS Filtering** (`ASMINUSXS`)
- **Enhancement**: as_minus_xs.py now accepts `threads` parameter and passes to `pysam.AlignmentFile`
- **Module update**: Automatically uses `task.cpus` for parallel BAM I/O operations
- **Impact**: Significantly faster read filtering for alignment score-based quality control
- **Implementation**: Line 30 in main.nf passes `${task.cpus}` to Python script

#### 4. **Parallelized Variant Calling** (`CALLING_VARDICT`)
- **Dynamic chunking**: Target BED file automatically split into `task.cpus` equal chunks
- **Parallel execution**:
  - Multiple `vardict-java` processes run simultaneously (one per chunk)
  - Parallel `teststrandbias.R` or AWK filtering per chunk
  - Background job management with proper error handling
- **Workflow**:
  1. Split target regions → Run VarDict per chunk → Concatenate raw TSV
  2. Apply statistical filters in parallel → Merge VCF headers/bodies → Final filtering
- **Result**: Near-linear speedup with CPU count for variant calling step
- **Code location**: Lines 38-109 in main.nf

---

### 📊 Resource Management Improvements

#### Configuration Updates
- **New config**: wide_panel.config for high-throughput panel sequencing
- **Refactored labels**: base.config now uses descriptive process-specific labels:
  - `process_memory_intensive` for AS-XS filtering
  - `process_very_high` for variant calling
  - Granular CPU/memory/time allocations per process type
- **Global resource limits**: Increased max limits in both config files to support parallel processing
- **Module-specific tuning**: Per-process resource assignments in modules.config including `SPLITBAMCHROM.*` configuration

#### Multi-threading Enhancements
- **samtools operations**: Added `--threads` / `-@ $task.cpus` flags to:
  - `samtools sort`, `samtools view`, `samtools index` in multiple modules
  - `bgzip` compression operations
- **Example**: `CLIPBAM` (line 32) and `COUNT_NS` (line 24) now use multi-threaded sorting

---

### 📝 Documentation & Testing

#### Documentation
- **Usage guide** (input_scenarios.md):
  - Section 5: "Performance Optimization (Chromosome Splitting)" with usage examples
  - Compatible with all input scenarios
  - Performance recommendations (enable for >50 samples)
- **Test documentation** (README.md):
  - Test 2: Chromosome-based parallelization validation
  - Test 3: Combined technical replicates + chromosome splitting
  - Tagged tests for selective execution: `nf-test test --tag "split_by_chrom"`

#### Test Coverage
- **nf-test suite** (main.nf.test):
  - Test with `split_by_chrom = true` validates correctness
  - Test with `splitted_original_sample = true` + `split_by_chrom = true` validates combined scenario
  - Ensures parallel processing produces identical results to sequential

---

### 🔧 Additional Improvements

#### Input Validation & Metadata
- **Fixed**: `fgbio/fastqtobam` now uses `meta.sample` instead of `meta.id` for proper sample/library assignment
- **New input format**: Lane-specific CSV support (`input_example_lanes.csv`) for multi-file workflows

#### Process Improvements
- **CALLING_VARDICT**: 
  - Conditional `teststrandbias` vs. AWK filter based on `params.use_teststrandbias`
  - Improved error handling with proper exit codes for parallel jobs
  - Better logging at each processing stage
- **SPLITBAMCHROM**: 
  - Robust reference filtering using `samtools idxstats` + `grep` patterns
  - Handles edge cases (chromosomes with no reads, unknown sequences)
  - Detailed per-chromosome statistics output

---

### ⚠️ Migration Notes

#### New Parameters
- `--split_by_chrom` (default: `false`): Enable chromosome-based parallelization
- `--use_teststrandbias` (affects variant calling filter method)

#### Configuration
- If using custom configs, review new process labels in base.config
- Consider adopting wide_panel.config for large panel sequencing projects

#### Performance Tuning
- Enable `--split_by_chrom true` for datasets with >50 samples or whole-exome/panel sequencing
- Ensure sufficient executor parallelism (e.g., `executor.queueSize` in nextflow.config)
- Allocate appropriate resources per process based on new labels

---

### 🎯 Performance Impact

**Expected improvements with `--split_by_chrom` enabled:**
- **Consensus calling**: ~25x parallelization (for human samples)
- **Variant calling**: Linear speedup with `task.cpus` (tested up to 32 CPUs)
- **AS-XS filtering**: 3-5x faster with multi-threaded I/O
- **Overall pipeline**: 40-60% reduction in wall-clock time for typical exome datasets

**Memory efficiency:**
- Per-chromosome processing reduces peak memory by ~90% (1/25th of genome per job)
- Enables processing of large cohorts on standard HPC nodes

---

### ✅ Testing & Validation

All changes validated through:
- nf-test suite with chromosome splitting enabled
- Comparison of split vs. non-split results (identical variants called)
- Resource monitoring to confirm parallel execution
- Multi-sample, multi-lane input scenarios

---

This PR maintains backward compatibility (all new features are opt-in via parameters) while providing significant performance improvements for users processing large duplex sequencing datasets.

author: lucas-gerard
body:
> Cette _pull request_ a été ouverte sans ticket Jira associé 👎

Dans cette PR :

# Suppression de l'utilisation du groupe de sérialisation InvoiceSerializationGroup::EXPAND_INVOICE

Utilisé uniquement par les endpoints Expert.
Après consultation de Damien côté front, le label sur les factures n'est nécessaire que sur les endpoints `App\Product\Accounting\Expert\Api\Endpoint\Invoicing\Invoice\GetInvoicesEndpoint` et `App\Product\Accounting\Expert\Api\Endpoint\BankTransaction\GetBankTransactionInvoicesEndpoint`.

Pour le premier cas, il a été géré dans #29741.
Pour le 2eme, la sérialisation semble passer par `InvoiceNormalizer`, classe modifiée dans cette PR (voir suite).

# Suppression de la propriété `$label` dans `Invoice`

Pour sérialiser cette propriété sur les invoices, on passe par de multiples méthodes (cf. `PieceHandler`) qui ont pour but d'appeler le setter `setLabel` sur l'entité `Invoice`. C'est la seule manière de renseigner cette propriété : elle n'est pas mappée via Doctrine.

Le getter est uniquement appelé dans l'`InvoiceNormalizer`. 
Puisque les méthodes du `PieceHandler` ne sont JAMAIS appelées avant l'utilisation de ce normalizer, la propriété `$label` de l'entité `Invoice` est constamment `NULL` lors de l'exécution, d'où la modification dans le normalizer (alternative proposée en commentaire de code si besoin).

Etant donné les éléments précédents, la propriété $label peut être éliminée de la classe `Invoice` :broom:

author: eileenmcnaughton
body:
Overview
----------------------------------------
Fix float precision edge case (server dependent)

In some cases the value php holds when it goes to save the Contribution is different to the value that is actually saved due to precision rounding This relates to the serialize_precision ini variable but appears to also have some other factors impacting it.

We have 3 places where we conditionally try to load a contribution once saved so it is useful to know that it is always retrieved and seems worth any trade off. On the other side if we retrieve it right after save we can unset the values that might cause inaccuracies


Before
----------------------------------------
In some circumstances we can wind up with a contribution with an amount field that is being rounded when saved in the contribution BAO due to floats being weird. In this case the `$contribution->find()` may not retrieve it causing failure when the activity is to be sent

After
----------------------------------------
Contribution is re-loaded straight after save in all cases. Amount fields are removed to prevent rounding mismatches

Technical Details
----------------------------------------
I was unable to replicate this with a pure float locally but could with a string. However, on our server it appears to be happening with a string...

Comments
----------------------------------------

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
🎯 Overview

This PR introduces a comprehensive patient safety monitoring system that transforms RxChain into a full pharmacovigilance platform. Patients can now register allergies, and pharmacies can report adverse events—creating an immutable safety record that prevents dangerous drug combinations and enables regulatory compliance.

## ✨ What's New

### Patient Allergies Registry
- **register-patient-allergy**: Patients self-register known allergies with severity levels (0-3)
- **get-allergy**: Query allergy details by ID
- **check-allergy-for-patient**: Verify ownership of allergy records
- **get-patient-allergy-count**: Track total allergies for audit trails

### Adverse Event Reporting
- **report-adverse-event**: Pharmacies document side effects with full prescription context
- **get-adverse-event**: Retrieve event details by ID
- **get-patient-event-count**: Monitor total reported incidents

### Supporting Functions
- **has-patient-allergies**: System-wide allergy status check
- **get-patient-allergy-count / get-patient-event-count**: Audit and compliance reporting

## 🛡️ Security Enhancements

- **Immutable Records**: Append-only allergies & events (no modifications/deletions)
- **Role-Based Access**: Patients register own allergies, pharmacies report events, doctors query
- **Bounded Validation**: All inputs length-checked, severity levels 0-3
- **Accountable Reporting**: Events tied to specific pharmacies with timestamps


## 🔄 Integration

- ✅ Zero breaking changes to existing functions
- ✅ Compatible with existing role-based permissions
- ✅ Seamless composition with prescription management
- ✅ Shared patient registry for consistency


## 📋 Use Cases

### Patient Safety Pre-Fill

author: rafaelfersilva
body:
Para execução dos testes com o banco precisamos criar um service no gitactions para excutar o banco de teste

```yaml
name: Pull Request CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  pull_requests:
    permissions: write-all
    name: PULL REQUESTS TESTS
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    services:
      mysql:
        image: mysql:8.0
        ports:
          - "3306:3306"
        env:
          MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD }}
          MYSQL_DATABASE: ${{ secrets.MYSQL_DATABASE }}
          MYSQL_USER: ${{ secrets.MYSQL_USER }}
          MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MYSQL_PASSWORD }}
        options: >-
          --health-cmd="mysqladmin ping --host=localhost --user=root --password=rootpassword"
          --health-interval=10s
          --health-timeout=5s
          --health-retries=5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout the test repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22.17.0"

      - name: Cache pip
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('**/requirements.txt') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

      - name: Install Requirements
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -U -r requirements.txt
          npx playwright install-deps

      - name: Init Browser Library
        run: rfbrowser init

      - name: Run the tests
        run: invoke test-pr

      - name: Validate Test Coverage
        if: always()
        id: test_coverage
        run: |
          python ./resources/libs/test_coverage_validator.py \
            ./reports/output.xml \
            --min-pass_rate 80 \
            --output-dir ./reports/pass_rate || exit 1

      - name: Read Markdown Report
        id: read_report
        if: always()
        run: |
          report_file=$(ls ./reports/pass_rate/test_pass_rate_report_*.md | head -n 1)
          echo "report_path=$report_file" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          cat $report_file

      - name: Create GitHub Comment
        if: always()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN}}
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const reportPath = '${{ steps.read_report.outputs.report_path }}';
            const reportContent = fs.readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8');

            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: reportContent
            });

      - name: Upload PR Artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pr-test-results
          path: |
            ./reports
            ./reports/coverage
            ./reports/robotmetrics
          retention-days: 5
          if-no-files-found: ignore

```

author: dragospe
body:
This is a quick fix for signature handling, but it's not perfect.

The issue was that we were adding the mock signatures before balancing and removing them after, but _before running validators_. 

This means that sizing calculations would not take the signatures into account, and this was causing test failures in hydrozoa when attempting to pack payouts into a settlement transaction.

One current issue with the way dummy signatures are handled is that it doesn't take into account the actual `expectedSigners` of the context. This means it might add a dummy signature for a signature that is actually present. And with this fix, if _all_ necessary signatures were present, the transaction would still fail the validation step since the dummy signatures are added regardless.

body:
The main workflow is now focused on building and testing across all supported networks for pull requests, and a separate workflow enables releases to be triggered manually. The release process now also creates a GitHub release.

**Workflow improvements:**

* The main workflow (`.github/workflows/main.yml`) is restructured to only run build and test jobs on pull request events, building all network variants instead of just mainnet. The automatic release job on push is removed.
* The previous `main_test.yml` workflow file is renamed to `release_on_demand.yml` and updated to allow manual (on-demand) releases via the GitHub Actions UI.

**Release process enhancements:**

* The manual release workflow now includes the `--github_release` flag in the publish command to automatically create a GitHub release when publishing.

author: joseriyancyriac
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the 3D visualization and UI for the base station app, focusing on enhanced visual clarity, better feedback for device connectivity, and improved command visualization. The most important changes include a major redesign of the header and layout, improved connection line rendering based on signal strength, and the addition of interactive command visualizations for device deployments.

**UI and Layout Enhancements:**
* Redesigned the header in `style.css` for a cleaner look, including fixed positioning, logo alignment, and improved title styling. Adjusted container and control layouts for better usability and visual structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c4609858ad578d3c821f7b22431d3a97f6d3077f130e115af1fc87e05b2bd495R6-R68) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c4609858ad578d3c821f7b22431d3a97f6d3077f130e115af1fc87e05b2bd495R117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c4609858ad578d3c821f7b22431d3a97f6d3077f130e115af1fc87e05b2bd495L40-R91)
* Improved matrix table color coding for signal strengths, introducing new classes for weak-medium and medium strengths for clearer feedback.
* Updated page title in `app.py` for branding consistency.

**Visualization and Connection Rendering:**
* Overhauled connection line rendering in `main.js` to use thick cylinder geometry, with color and dash patterns based on RSSI values. Lines are now colored (red, orange, yellow, green) and dashed for weak connections, providing immediate visual feedback on link quality. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacR284-R293) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL311-R646) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL296-R304)
* Connection thresholds are now configurable and consistent with matrix display, and connection logic is more robust.

**Device and Model Handling:**
* Updated device model configuration to improve positioning and scaling, and changed the base station display to use the AGV2 model for better visual distinction. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL32-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL136-R136) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL209-R211)
* Ground grid and plane visuals are now more subtle and transparent for improved depth perception.

**Command Visualization Feature:**
* Added interactive command visualization: when a deployment command is issued, a translucent sphere appears at the target location, with ghost lines and labels indicating predicted signal strength to the base and served devices. Visualizations are removed automatically when the device reaches the target. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacR251-R253) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL311-R646) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL296-R304)
* Includes helper functions for signal prediction, text label creation, dashed ghost lines, and completion checks, making deployment feedback much clearer for users. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacL311-R646) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-508b7c6356ae95743670e754fb53da74bde2cb7a49eee15a6d0cb58e634dadacR251-R253)

These changes collectively provide a more intuitive, informative, and visually appealing experience for users interacting with the 6G TakeOff visualization.

author: omgitsraven
body: I'm working on a Lua script to track whether a player has seen all possible text in the game; it checks based on reads to CCS text block start addresses.  But because some blocks have conditional branches in their middles, the non-branching option at the ends of those blocks weren't being acknowledged as something unseen.   Using the new -s flag that I've added here will produce a dump where a new block is started whenever a conditional jump control code is encountered, so that "blocks" (in this mode) are only ever a chunk of text that's guaranteed to be printed in its entirety.

author: laurensmiers
body:
MCPP fails to compile due to stricter checks in newer compiles.

First error is regarding a mismatch of argument expectations:
```
mcpp_main.c: In function ‘mcpp_lib_main’:
mcpp_main.c:305:5: error: too many arguments to function ‘mb_init’; expected 0, have 1
  305 |     mb_init(TRUE);      /* Should be initialized prior to get options   */
      |     ^~~~~~~
In file included from mcpp_main.c:39:
internal.H:419:17: note: declared here
  419 | extern void     mb_init();
      |                 ^~~~~~~
make: *** [<builtin>: mcpp_main.o] Error 1
```

Second error is regarding the use of reserved keywords for goto-labels:
```
system.c: In function ‘open_file’:
system.c:1741:15: error: expected identifier or ‘*’ before ‘true’
 1741 |         goto  true;
      |               ^~~~
system.c:1768:19: error: expected identifier or ‘*’ before ‘false’
 1768 |             goto  false;
      |                   ^~~~~
system.c:1773:15: error: expected identifier or ‘*’ before ‘false’
 1773 |         goto  false;
      |               ^~~~~
system.c:1805:5: error: expected ‘;’ before ‘:’ token
 1805 | true:
      |     ^
      |     ;
system.c:1807:6: error: expected ‘;’ before ‘:’ token
 1807 | false:
      |      ^
      |      ;
make: *** [<builtin>: system.o] Error 1
```

When both of these are tackled, mcpp compilation succeeds using GCC 15.22.1:
```bash
$ cc --version
cc (GCC) 15.2.1 20250813
$ make
$ ls lib64/libmcpp.a
lib64/libmcpp.a
```

This was also flagged in the original mcpp, but no fix accepted yet:
https://sourceforge.net/p/mcpp/bugs/18/

This fix is necessary if we want to install zeroc-ice pypi package since on Linux, the backend is build and these errors pop-up.
